title: React application and authentication
description: Project: React application and authentication. Build and understand this project with step-by-step guidance.

data.text: The React frontend for a real-time communication platform must handle authentication, optimistic UI updates, message state, and connection lifecycle events without blocking the main thread. Senior engineers treat the frontend as a distributed system participant: it has local state, remote state, eventual consistency, and failure modes that must be visible to users.

items: Use server-side session cookies or signed JWTs for WebSocket authentication during the upgrade request
Store auth state in React context or a state manager and trigger a global re-auth flow on 401 responses
Apply optimistic updates for message sending to make the UI feel instant, with rollback on failure
Manage WebSocket connection state with a dedicated hook that exposes readyState and reconnect status
Use React Query or SWR to cache messages and synchronize with the server on reconnect
Debounce typing indicators to avoid flooding the message bus with redundant events
Handle token expiration: silent refresh or redirect to login without losing unsent message drafts

terms.definition: Updating the local UI state before the server confirms the operation, then rolling back if the request fails.
Refreshing an expired auth token in the background using a refresh token without user interaction.
The state of the local UI may temporarily diverge from the server but will converge after synchronization.
The current status of a WebSocket connection: connecting, open, closing, or closed.
Delaying an action until a specified quiet period has elapsed, reducing the rate of repeated events like typing indicators.

data.text: A frontend that does not handle auth expiration or failed optimistic updates will create a fragmented experience where users see duplicate messages, lost drafts, or frozen UIs. Senior engineers build frontend state machines that handle every connection state and auth edge case, so the application degrades gracefully rather than crashing.

data.title: Use a state machine for connection state
data.text: Model the WebSocket connection as a finite state machine with states: idle, connecting, connected, reconnecting, disconnected. Do not use a simple boolean. A state machine makes it easy to render the correct UI and prevents impossible transitions like sending while disconnected.

items: Cookie-based session: server sets an HTTP-only cookie after login; WebSocket upgrade inherits the cookie automatically
Bearer token in query string: convenient but less secure; tokens may leak in server logs
Subprotocol token: pass the token in the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header during upgrade
Refresh token rotation: issue short-lived access tokens and long-lived refresh tokens; rotate refresh tokens on each use

items: Cache messages in a normalized store keyed by message ID to support fast lookup and updates
Synchronize on reconnect by requesting missed messages from the server using a last-known message ID cursor
Handle message ordering conflicts by preferring the server-assigned timestamp or sequence number
Show a visual indicator when the connection is reconnecting so users understand why new messages are not appearing
Persist unsent drafts to IndexedDB or localStorage so they survive page refreshes

data.title: Build an auth-aware WebSocket hook
data.description: Create a useWebSocket hook that manages authentication, reconnection, and message state for a chat application. The hook should expose sendMessage, messages, connectionState, and a readyState getter.
steps: Implement the WebSocket connection with upgrade authentication
Add heartbeat and reconnect logic with exponential backoff
Use React Query to cache messages and synchronize on reconnect
Implement optimistic message sending with rollback on failure
Handle token expiration by showing a login modal without losing draft messages
data.expectedOutcome: You should have a production-ready hook that handles auth, reconnection, and optimistic updates without blocking the UI.

items.question: Should I store the JWT in localStorage?
items.answer: Prefer HTTP-only cookies for access tokens to prevent XSS. If you must use localStorage, ensure you have strict Content Security Policy headers and do not expose the token to third-party scripts.

items.question: How do I handle message duplication after reconnect?
items.answer: Use a client-generated message ID as an idempotency key. The server should deduplicate based on that key. On reconnect, the client can re-send unacknowledged messages and the server will ignore duplicates.

items.question: What if React Query cache becomes stale?
items.answer: React Query automatically invalidates stale data on window focus and reconnect. For real-time updates, use the WebSocket message stream to update the cache directly with queryClient.setQueryData.

data.title: Summary
points: Treat the frontend as a distributed participant with eventual consistency
Use optimistic updates with rollback for instant feedback
Model connection state explicitly with a state machine
Handle auth expiration without losing user work
data.takeaway: A senior frontend engineer designs for failure and recovery first, then adds features. The best real-time UIs feel instant because they handle network latency gracefully.
